newsitem.title: MEXICO: At least 18 dead in two Mexico crashes.
newsitem.headline: At least 18 dead in two Mexico crashes.

text.p: Fourteen people riding in the back of a pickup truck were killed when the vehicle crashed in central Mexico on New Year's Day, police said on Thursday.

In a seperate accident, at least four people died and 56 were injured when four tourist buses crashed early on Thursday on the main Mexico City-Acapulco highway near the city of Cuernavaca, officials said.
Local government officials in the north-central city of Leon said the victims in the truck crash all belonged to an extended family on a religious pilgrimage.

"We have a report of an accident involving a pickup truck on the Leon-Lagos highway with a tragic result of 14 people dead and eight injured," Ruben Torres, an officer with the Federal Highway Police in Leon, told reporters.
TV images showed the front end of the truck completely destroyed at the side of a straight stretch of the highway.
In the other crash, four buses ran into each other close to the city of Cuernavaca in the state of Morelos, Jesus Hernandez, a spokesman for the state of Morelos, said.

The bus pile up occurred in the early morning of Thursday in dark and foggy conditions, on a windy stretch of road and on a steep decline, Hernandez said. The buses all were headed south on the toll road to the Pacific coast resort.
